findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow uses raw String status plus independent bool flags (is_validated, is_sent) and Option<u64> sent_at_epoch_ms, allowing every invalid combination: status='sent' with is_sent=false, is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None, status='validated' with is_validated=false, etc.
findings.failure_mode: Any code that checks item.is_sent without also checking item.status can act on a lease that was never actually sent. Conversely, checking status string alone misses the lifecycle data. These booleans are shape-level invariants that the compiler cannot enforce.
findings.fix: Replace status/is_validated/is_sent/sent_at_epoch_ms with a single enum typestate like enum LeaseState { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } } where each variant owns its lifecycle data. Remove all bool/Option fields.

findings.problem: pub status: String allows arbitrary values ("sent", "SENT", "", "pending", "foo") with no compiler-enforced set of valid states.
findings.failure_mode: Typo in status comparison, case mismatch, or unexpected string value silently bypasses state checks. Runtime string comparison is slower than enum discriminant comparison.
findings.fix: Replace with an enum: pub enum LeaseStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } and remove is_sent and is_validated booleans which become redundant discriminant checks.

findings.problem: pub id: String allows any string including empty, whitespace, or non-lease-id values to be used as an identifier. String is interchangeable with other string fields.
findings.failure_mode: Accidental swap between id and status strings at call sites. Empty or malformed IDs pass through without validation. No domain-level id invariants (format, length, uniqueness) are enforced at the type level.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype: pub struct LeaseId(String) with a smart constructor that validates the id format and returns a typed error. Replace pub id: String with pub id: LeaseId.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes and returns LeaseWorkflow by value, mutating raw fields directly (item.status = "sent".to_string(); item.is_sent = true). This leaks primitive mutation into what should be an explicit state transition.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set status and is_sent independently, creating invalid intermediate states. The function performs two mutations atomically at the call site but provides no typed guarantee that both will always happen together. No failure case is modeled.
findings.fix: Change mark_sent to a method on the typestate enum that returns Result<LeaseState, LeaseError> with a transition variant like fn transition_to_sent(self, epoch_ms: u64) -> Result<LeaseState, CannotTransition>.

findings.problem: No smart constructor or From/Into impl exists. Callers can construct LeaseWorkflow with { id: "".into(), status: "".into(), is_validated: false, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None }, an obviously invalid initial state.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code must re-validate every field on every access. The invalid state can propagate through the system until a bug manifests at an unrelated call site.
findings.fix: Add a private constructor or a builder with smart constructor logic: fn new(id: LeaseId) -> Result<LeaseWorkflow, InvalidLease> that returns the initial valid state (Pending).

findings.problem: pub sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a global Option on the struct rather than owned by the Sent lifecycle variant. is_sent == true with sent_at_epoch_ms == None is a valid struct but semantically broken (sent but no timestamp).
findings.failure_mode: Code that assumes sent leases always have a timestamp will get None and must handle it, or silently produce incorrect downstream calculations (e.g., lease age, expiration).
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into a Sent variant: enum LeaseState { Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. The type system guarantees the timestamp exists when the state is Sent.

findings.problem: mark_sent returns LeaseWorkflow directly with no error type. There is no way to represent failure (e.g., lease already sent, lease not yet validated).
findings.failure_mode: Missing validation of preconditions (e.g., is_validated must be true before sent) means invalid transitions silently succeed. Future transitions cannot be modeled without changing the return type.
findings.fix: Define a typed error enum: pub enum LeaseError { AlreadySent, NotValidated, InvalidTransition { from: LeaseStatus, to: LeaseStatus } } and return Result<LeaseWorkflow, LeaseError>.

findings.problem: All fields of LeaseWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to bypass all state transitions and mutate status/is_validated/is_sent directly.
findings.failure_mode: External callers can create invalid states by mutating fields directly, e.g., item.is_sent = true without updating status or sent_at_epoch_ms.
findings.fix: Make fields private, provide immutable accessors, and only expose state transition methods. Or replace with an enum typestate where variants are inherently immutable.

missing_evidence: no benchmark directory or benchmark files exist for any performance claim
no profiler evidence exists for allocation patterns in LeaseWorkflow construction or transitions
no allocation analysis: mark_sent performs .to_string() allocation on status every call
no second-ring evidence (proptest, fuzz, Kani, property tests) for state-transition invariants
no command evidence: no cargo test, cargo check, or cargo clippy output present
no behavior tests exist to verify state transition invariants
no command-line tool or CLI exists for the workflow
residual_risk: High. The domain model represents every possible boolean/string combination as valid, including states that violate lease lifecycle invariants. The type system provides zero enforcement of the actual business rules. Without enum typestates, any caller can construct or mutate a LeaseWorkflow into an impossible state. The missing benchmarks, tests, and clippy gates leave resource usage and correctness unverified.
